rules.message: jest has no expect.poll, so this throws or passes without checking. Poll in a loop with a deadline (the repo's poll helper), or move the test to Playwright.
networkidle waits for every request to stop, so it hangs or passes early on pages with live updates. Wait for what the test needs: await expect(locator).toBeVisible(), or page.waitForResponse(url).

this case plants a fixed date and reads the real clock, so it passes for a day and then fails everywhere. Fake the clock (jest.useFakeTimers().setSystemTime(...)), pass `now` all the way down, or place the dates from the real clock.

A fixed sleep waits a set time, so it's too short on a slow runner and wasted time on a fast one. Wait for a state instead: await expect(locator).toBeVisible(), toHaveText(…), or page.waitForResponse(url).

A pick by position (.nth(), .first(), .last(), :nth-child, rows[2]) breaks when the order changes but the page still works. Pick by what it is: getByRole(role, { name }), getByLabel(…), getByTestId(…), or locator.filter({ hasText }).
A styling class in a selector breaks when the CSS is renamed but the page still works. Use getByRole(role, { name }), getByLabel(…), or a data-testid the page keeps for tests.

This bounds real elapsed time under 1 s, so it fails on a busy runner with nothing wrong. Use fake timers, or assert the order of events. If time must be measured, use a bound of 1 s or more, with the bad path seconds away.

This comment records history (an issue or PR number, who asked and when, or what the code was before). Put history in the commit message and the PR. Keep a comment only for a constraint the code can't show, and prefer a test for it.

This change adds comment lines: the count across the files it touched, new files included, went up. Say it in the code (a clearer name, a smaller function, a test), or put it in the commit and the PR. Nothing excuses this rule: to add a comment, remove one in the files you change. Moving a comment between files, new ones included, is fine; the count is per change.
a closing keyword closes the issue with no proof it works. Write Refs #N; the issue closes with a live-proof comment.
